title: Near enough to hear, generous enough to answer
subtitle: Al-Mujib: the Responder, who answers every sincere call in the way that is best
intro: Al-Mujib (الْمُجِيبُ) means the Responder: the One who answers those who call on Him, meets requests with giving and desperation with rescue, and is near to every servant who turns to Him. It means no sincere prayer is wasted: every dua is answered, either as you asked, or with something better, or by protection you never saw.

root.sense: Jawb is to cut through or pierce, as Thamud carved through rock in the valley (89:9). Ijabah, a response, is a reply that cuts through the distance between a question and its answer. Al-Mujib is the One whose answer reaches you, however far away you feel.

row.title: Every sincere dua is answered
sub: in His way, at His time

knowing: Many people are close to us but not responsive. A cousin, a friend, even a best friend may say they are busy when you need them. Al-Mujib is near and He responds. My Lord is near and responsive, said the Prophet Salih (11:61). {idea}Closeness and response together: that is what makes Him the One to call.{/idea}

Look at how Allah speaks about prayer in the middle of the verses on fasting. Elsewhere, when people ask the Prophet ﷺ something, Allah says: tell them. Here He says: when My servants ask you about Me, I am near; I respond to the call of the caller when he calls (2:186). There is no tell them in between. {idea}He answers directly, and He calls them My servants.{/idea}

His answer is not like a vending machine. He responds with perfect knowledge and wisdom. The Prophet ﷺ said that whenever a Muslim makes a dua that contains no sin or cutting of family ties, Allah gives him one of three: He answers it soon, saves it for him in the Hereafter, or turns away an equal harm from him (Musnad Ahmad). Nothing sincere is wasted.
seeing: Zakariyya was old, his bones weak, his hair white, and his wife had never had children. He called his Lord in a quiet, private voice and said he had never been disappointed in calling Him (19:3-4). Allah answered him and gave him Yahya (21:90). He did not order a result; he poured out his heart.

Nuh called and Allah answered him and saved him from the flood (21:76). Ayyub called in his illness and Allah removed his suffering and gave back his family (21:84). Yunus called from the darkness inside the whale and Allah answered and saved him, and so He saves the believers (21:88). Who else answers the desperate when they call and removes the harm (27:62)?

Ibrahim left his family in a barren valley and asked Allah to turn people's hearts toward them and provide for them (14:37). Every crowd in Makkah today, every fruit in its markets, is part of the answer to one man's prayer.
trusting: We sometimes treat dua like online shopping: add to basket, expect delivery in three days, complain when it is late. {trap}Treating dua as a transaction{/trap} makes us give up. The Prophet ﷺ said your dua is answered as long as you are not hasty and say: I prayed but I was not answered (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Keep asking. The asking itself is worship.

Ask honestly and boldly. Be raw with Him, like Zakariyya. Do not be shy to ask for big things; Sulayman asked for a kingdom like no one after him (38:35). You are asking the One whose treasures never run out.

And when the answer looks like no, remember the three ways He responds. {reward}The thing you did not get may have been exchanged for something better, or for a harm you will never know you escaped.{/reward}
loving: Imagine a friend who always picks up, at any hour, and never tires of hearing from you. Al-Mujib is more than that. {idea}He asks you to call, and He is pleased when you do.{/idea}
Love grows each time you look back and see a prayer He answered, sometimes years later, sometimes in a form you did not expect, always with care.
now: It is the last third of the night. The house is asleep, and you have been asking for the same thing for two years, a child, a job, a cure. You almost did not get up tonight. {reward}Al-Mujib has heard every one of those prayers, and none of them was wasted.{/reward} Raise your hands again, tell Him everything, and ask big.
old: I have asked so many times; maybe my prayers are just not being heard.
new: Al-Mujib answers every sincere dua in the best way and time, so I keep asking with hope.
try: Pick one dua you had given up on and make it again today, with full attention, raising your hands.

dua.text: Ya Mujib, You are near and You answer. Answer my call, give me what is good for me, turn away what would harm me, and never let me tire of asking You.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name in the last third of the night and in moments of desperation; He promised: call on Me and I will respond to you (40:60).

pairs.why: As-Sami' hears every call and Al-Mujib answers it; hearing that leads to response.
Al-Mujib answers, Al-Karim answers generously, often giving more than was asked.
Al-Mujib responds to your asking; Al-Wahhab gives freely, even without being asked (38:35).

faq.a: Al-Mujib means the Responder. Allah answers those who call on Him, meets requests with giving and desperation with rescue. He is described as near and responsive in 11:61, and He says I respond to the call of the caller in 2:186.

faq.q: Why do some duas seem unanswered?
faq.a: According to a hadith in Musnad Ahmad, every sincere dua free of sin is answered in one of three ways: granted soon, saved for the Hereafter, or an equal harm is turned away. The Prophet ﷺ also warned against being hasty and giving up (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

faq.q: What is the connection between Al-Mujib and Ramadan?
faq.a: The verse I am near; I respond to the call of the caller (2:186) comes in the middle of the verses about fasting in Surah al-Baqarah. Many scholars see this placement as an encouragement to make abundant dua during Ramadan.
